comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
RETRACTION -- THIS TICKET IS FACTUALLY WRONG AS FILED, and I filed it. Verified against current main in a venv worktree rather than from memory.

MY CLAIM WAS: 'a mechanism-ok marker satisfies --check but NOT tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py, which asserts new == 0 and set(baseline) == live REGARDLESS of markers, and every route to the baseline is forbidden to contributors -- therefore no justified mechanism is landable.'

BOTH ASSERTIONS ACTUALLY HONOUR MARKERS. Read them:
  test_check_passes_on_the_committed_tree:
      assert "new=0" in out or "admitted" in out
  test_the_committed_baseline_matches_the_live_tree (line 349):
      assert set(baseline) | admitted == live
The first passes on an 'admitted' line; the second adds the admitted set explicitly. So a correctly
marked mechanism needs no baseline entry and no maintenance command.

PROOF ON CURRENT MAIN: the scanner-integration workflow carries two ci_gate markers, the committed
baseline contains ZERO scanner entries (grep -c = 0), --check reports 'active=682 new=2 increased=0
stale=0' with BOTH lines marked 'admitted', and both assertions PASS. That is precisely the situation
this ticket says is impossible.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED WITH CHANGE 2601 is narrower and I over-generalised from it. Its failure was:
  FAILED test_check_passes_on_the_committed_tree - AssertionError: active=682 new=1 increased=0 stale=0
Note the output has NO 'admitted' line. Its marker was NOT matched by markers_for -- compare.py:95
requires a marker for the EXACT key. So the real question is why that one marker did not match
(placement or parse), not whether markers work at all. We never diagnosed it, because that agent
restructured to avoid the mechanism entirely -- partly on my say-so.

THE COST OF MY ERROR, recorded because it changed real decisions:
 - Change 2601 restructured its design to dodge a mechanism it may not have needed to dodge. The
   restructure is defensible on its own merits (repairing the existing guard is narrower than adding
   a second one beside it) but it was chosen under a false constraint.
 - The S6 agent DECLINED to add the REBAR_GATE_MAX_CONCURRENT env tier that ADR 0112 asks for,
   citing this contradiction, and documented the omission as a deviation to be revisited 'once a1f1
   is fixed'. There is nothing to fix, so that tier can simply be added with a correct marker.
 - Every subagent brief tonight carried 'you cannot land a new mechanism -- STOP and report'. That
   instruction was wrong and is now withdrawn.

RESCOPING THIS TICKET rather than closing it outright: there IS a real, much smaller defect here --
a marker can silently fail to match its key, and when it does, the failure message says 'new=1' with
no hint that a marker was present but rejected. That is a bad diagnostic for an easy mistake.
Proposed replacement acceptance criteria:
 1. A mechanism-ok marker that does not match any detected key produces a diagnostic naming the
    marker, the key it was parsed as, and the keys actually detected -- rather than silently leaving
    the mechanism unadmitted.
 2. Reproduce 2601's exact marker and determine why it was not admitted; fix the cause if it is a
    parser/placement defect, or document the rule if the marker was genuinely malformed.
 3. docs/architecture.md's 'Mechanism-delta ratchet' section states marker placement per detection
    shape unambiguously, since ci_gate has TWO shapes (scripts/check_*.py named by path, and workflow
    run: steps named by file::step) and they plainly do not take a marker in the same place.
 4. Defect-seeded: a deliberately malformed marker makes AC1's diagnostic fire.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Live evidence for this ticket's REAL defect (silent non-admission), from change 2658 tonight.

An agent implementing `fd2b` + `eebc` added two justified mechanisms with `# mechanism-ok:` markers
at their definition sites. Its report:

> `make verify` full suite: **19450 passed, 2 failed** — both `test_mechanism_delta.py`, because the
> two new mechanisms need baseline entries **in addition to** their `# mechanism-ok:` markers
> (`--update-stale` refuses to write while anything is new, so there is no other path). I added
> exactly those two lines to `.github/mechanism-baseline.json` — surgical insert, no unrelated churn.

That is a contributor hitting exactly the wall this ticket describes, and resolving it by
hand-editing a file `AGENTS.md` explicitly says not to hand-edit:

> Do **not** hand-edit `.github/mechanism-baseline.json`; `--update-stale` is maintenance-only, and
> it refuses to write at all while anything is new.

So the documented guidance and the observed behaviour disagree, and the contributor was left with
no sanctioned path. Note the shape: `--update-stale` refuses **because** something is new, and the
thing that is new is exactly what the marker was supposed to admit.

## What this does NOT establish

This ticket was already retracted once for a false premise, so I am being careful. This comment
does NOT re-open the retracted claim. The retraction established that a CORRECT marker satisfies
both assertions. Both of these remain live and untested here:

- **(a)** the agent's markers were malformed or did not match the detected `(kind, name)` key, and
  were therefore silently ignored — which IS this ticket's defect, and the marker's silence is why
  the agent could not tell; or
- **(b)** the markers were correct and something else requires the baseline entry — which would
  mean the retraction was itself incomplete.

Distinguishing them is cheap and worth doing before designing a fix: take change 2658's two
markers, revert its `.github/mechanism-baseline.json` edit, run
`python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` and `pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py`,
and see whether the markers alone admit the mechanisms. Whichever way it lands is a real finding —
and if it is (a), this ticket's acceptance criteria should require that a non-matching marker SAYS
SO rather than being ignored, since a silent marker is what turned a two-minute fix into a
guidance violation.

The change is 2658 (`1748404108c3`); the mechanisms are in the terraform-drift workflow work.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
VERDICT ON THE (a)/(b) FORK: it is **(b)**, and the cause is a COLLATERAL REVERT. Change 2658's markers were CORRECT. The retraction was true when written and was invalidated four commits later. This ticket needs rescoping again.

## The experiment

Worktree at origin/main `9d5a7278c892`. Deleted exactly the two lines change 2658 added to `.github/mechanism-baseline.json`, changed nothing else:

    $ python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check ; echo exit=$?
    active=680 new=2 increased=0 stale=0
      admitted  ci_gate::.github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml::Assert this tree is current with the tracked branch — bug eebc-6aa1-e45b-4325: ...
      admitted  ci_gate::scripts/check_terraform_tree_currency.py — bug eebc-6aa1-e45b-4325:
    exit=0

Both markers MATCHED. `--check` is green. So the markers were neither malformed nor mis-keyed — (a) is excluded as the cause.

    $ pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py -q
    2 failed, 30 passed
    FAILED test_check_passes_on_the_committed_tree - AssertionError: active=680 new=2 increased=0 stale=0
    FAILED test_the_committed_baseline_matches_the_live_tree - Extra items in the right set:
      'ci_gate::.github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml::Assert this tree is current with the tracked branch'
      'ci_gate::scripts/check_terraform_tree_currency.py'

With the two baseline lines restored (i.e. unmodified main): **32 passed**. So the two baseline lines were load-bearing and the marker alone does not satisfy the suite.

## Why the retraction disagrees: the assertions it quoted were REVERTED

The retraction quoted `assert "new=0" in out or "admitted" in out` and `assert set(baseline) | admitted == live`. Neither exists on main. Current main, `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py`:

    line  94:  assert "new=0" in out and "increased=0" in out, out
    line 358:  assert set(baseline) == live

`git log -S'admitted' -- tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` returns exactly two commits:

- **6125c5345f01** "Pin review scanner contracts in Verified" — ADDED the marker-honouring forms (it introduced two new `ci_gate` mechanisms, so it had to).
- **9c7d78127696** "Revert scanner-integration Verified gate" — reverted 6125c534 WHOLESALE, for reasons entirely unrelated to the ratchet (vacuous Verified vote; the new required job was red on main and blocking Verified +1 for every open change). The revert took the marker-honouring assertions with it and restored the marker-blind forms.

So the retraction's "PROOF ON CURRENT MAIN" was accurate at the moment it was observed, and was undone by 9c7d78 along with the workflow. AC2's own note spotted that the workflow was reverted and called the proof stale — but inferred only that the *proof* was stale, not that the *assertions* had been reverted too. That is the missed step.

**Net: on current main the ticket's ORIGINAL premise is true again.** A correctly-marked new mechanism passes `--check` and still fails two unit tests, and `--update-stale` refuses to write while anything is new. Change 2658's agent hit a real wall and had no sanctioned path; the hand-edit was the only route available. The AGENTS.md guidance and the tree genuinely disagree.

## The (a) defect is real, but latent and NOT what bit 2658

Independently confirmed by construction — a well-formed marker whose key matches no detected mechanism is entirely silent:

    >>> evaluate({"lock::a.lock":1}, {"lock::a.lock":1},
    ...          {"ci_gate::totally/wrong/key.py":"bug 1234 — justified"})
    exit: 0
    active=1 new=0 increased=0 stale=0

`compare.py` `_partition` reads `markers.get(key, "")`, and `_blank_marker_errors` only reports markers whose reason is blank. A non-blank marker on an unmatched key is never mentioned on any line. So silent non-admission exists and is worth fixing — but it would NOT have helped 2658, whose markers matched.

## Recommended rescoping

Two separable defects, and the current ACs describe only the second:

1. **PRIMARY (the live one, currently unticketed):** the two assertions in `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` are marker-blind because a revert swept away their marker-honouring forms. Fix = re-apply what 6125c5345f01 had (`markers_for` still exists and is exported, so this is a re-application, not a design). Add a regression test that pins the tests themselves to honour markers, so the next wholesale revert of an unrelated change cannot silently re-open this. That last part is the real lesson: the ratchet's marker contract was only ever expressed inside a commit that was revertable for other reasons.
2. **SECONDARY (this ticket's current ACs, still valid as written):** silent non-admission — a non-matching marker should name the key it was parsed as and the keys actually detected. Confirmed real above. Keep as-is, but it is a DX improvement, not the blocker.

AC2 as written ("reproduce 2601's marker and determine why it was not admitted") should note that 2601 predates this analysis and that 2658 — the case with live evidence — was NOT a marker defect.

I am NOT claiming this ticket: its ACs target (a), and an attestation against them would certify the wrong fix. Handing back for the rescoping decision. No code changed; scratch worktree only, main untouched.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Mechanism-ratchet archaeology (2026-09-06): design-free-fixable. The sanctioned path is already marker-only: `scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py` says `--check` exits 0 when every new/increased mechanism carries a non-blank exact-key `# mechanism-ok:` marker; `scripts/_mechanism_delta/compare.py:evaluate()` partitions new/increased keys into admitted/unadmitted using the marker map and returns 0 when only admitted regressions remain. `docs/architecture.md` §Mechanism-delta ratchet says `--update-stale` is maintenance-only and the contributor path is the marker or removing the mechanism.

The two unit-test invariants now pin that same contract: `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py::test_check_passes_on_the_committed_tree` accepts either `new=0` or `admitted`, and `test_the_committed_baseline_matches_the_live_tree` asserts `set(baseline) | admitted == live`. A source-level regression test at lines ~480-530 exists specifically because the marker-honouring assertions were once lost in a wholesale revert; it states that otherwise a correct marker fails the suite and hand-editing the baseline is the forbidden fallback.

Conclusion: making marker green imply tests green is a defect fix in the existing sanctioned path, not a new exception/bypass mechanism. No user design decision is needed unless an implementation proposes something other than exact-key marker admission + diagnostics for unmatched/miskeyed markers.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

The mechanism-delta ratchet has one sanctioned contributor path for a justified new mechanism: an exact-key, non-blank `# mechanism-ok:` marker at the detector-defined placement. The checker path already honors admitted markers, but the unit-test contract has previously drifted marker-blind after collateral reverts. The desired invariant is simple: marker green implies checker green and unit tests green, with no baseline edit and no new exception/bypass route.

Operator decision 2026-09-06: mechanisms must not require exception routes. The `# mechanism-ok:` marker is the sanctioned no-exception path. Fix marker admission/test consistency only; do not add override mechanisms and do not make `.github/mechanism-baseline.json` contributor-editable.

Current archaeology to respect:
- `scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exits 0 when all new/increased mechanisms are admitted by exact-key non-blank markers.
- `scripts/_mechanism_delta/compare.py:evaluate()` partitions new/increased keys into admitted/unadmitted using the marker map.
- `.github/workflows/_scanner-integration.yml` is present on current main and carries two workflow-step `ci_gate` markers; use that live fixture rather than claiming it is absent.
- The live defect class is a regression guard gap: marker-admitted mechanisms must satisfy both checker output expectations and `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` baseline-vs-live assertions.
- A separate DX issue exists for orphan or mis-keyed markers that are parsed nowhere; that can be split if it is larger than this marker-green/unit-green consistency fix.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A marker-admitted new mechanism satisfies `scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` and the relevant `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` unit tests without editing `.github/mechanism-baseline.json`.
- [ ] Regression coverage pins the unit-test contract itself: marker-admitted mechanisms are counted as admitted in the committed-tree output assertion and in the baseline-vs-live set equality assertion.
- [ ] The reproduction uses a current in-tree marker fixture where possible, including the present `.github/workflows/_scanner-integration.yml` workflow-step `ci_gate` markers, and does not rely on the stale claim that the workflow is absent.
- [ ] No new bypass, force, exception list, or contributor baseline-edit path is introduced; the only sanctioned path remains an exact-key non-blank `# mechanism-ok:` marker.

## Testing / Verification
- Add or strengthen tests in `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` that fail if marker-admitted mechanisms are omitted from either checker-output acceptance or baseline-vs-live comparison.
- Run `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest -q tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` and `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check`.
- Before pushing, run env -u GIT_CONFIG_COUNT -u GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0 -u GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0 -u GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1 -u GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1 -u GIT_CONFIG_KEY_2 -u GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2 PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make verify.
